show_hn.title: Show HN: Pizza – An event-driven AI agent, no while true
show_hn.story_text: Hi HN, I made Pizza, an open-source, event-driven AI agent. No `while true`. Each turn is a state machine. Conversations and tool calls go into an immutable SQLite log. The UI, model context, and session tree are built from that log. The model gets one tool: a CLI. Reading files, editing code, and running commands all go through it. You can keep a conversation going without manually starting new sessions. Pizza compacts context as needed, and you can branch from any earlier message. Agents in separate workspaces talk through `tell`, each doing the work in its own project. An SSH host can be a workspace too: Pizza deploys itself there and runs remotely. show_hn.story_text: Hi HN! profiler-md is a CLI and JS library that converts performance profiles to Markdown across 17 formats (e.g. pprof), 29 profilers (e.g. py-spy), 22 languages (e.g. Rust), and 4 profile types (call stack profiles, call graphs, heap snapshots, and traces). Earlier this year I tried using AI agents for performance optimization. They weren't very effective because they frequently: - Speculated about why something was slow from just reading the code - Made changes, measured the wall time before vs after, and struggled to distinguish real improvements from noise - Analyzed raw profiles using one-off scripts, which were often subtly incorrect The issue was that the agents couldn't read a flamegraph like I could. Show HN: Flipbook Foundry – animated stick figures baked into a font
show_hn.story_text: I've always loved flipbooks, the little stick figure running and jumping around the corner of a page. I was curious if I could hi-jack a font file with stick figure glyphs. So I prompted Flipbook Foundry into existence. Each animated frame of the a stick figure's motion is just a glyph in the font. You can drop {walk} into a paragraph and a stick figure walks right through it, at text size, and the words move aside. The text reflow runs on Cheng Lou's awesome pretext library, which is fast enough to animate everything performantly. There's an API for it (framer-motion style, for Svelte / React / plain JS), and the fonts are regular .otf files. Made a little demo page too - check it out and enjoy the swarm!

I wanted something where every device in the network can act as a self node, and it'll be a Mesh of devices interconnected. Further it also allowed me to keep internal names like nas.home.kith.internal, and exit nodes, relays... it's free and open source (AGPL), written in Rust It really felt useful to me so I just want to know what would make it further helpful? ...
